title: How to Calculate Your Office Administrator Salary: Hourly to Annual Guide
description: Convert your hourly rate to an annual office administrator salary using 38-hour weeks. Includes tax, super, and award rates from Fair Work Ombudsman.
salarySummary: For a full-time office administrator working 38 hours per week, the annual salary is approximately hourly rate × 38 × 52, with super paid on top and tax withheld according to 2026–27 rates.

faqs.q: What is the minimum hourly rate for an office administrator in 2026?
faqs.a: The minimum hourly rate depends on the applicable award. Most office administrators are covered by the Clerks Award (MA000031), which has classification levels starting above the National Minimum Wage. As of 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour for award-free employees. For award-covered employees, check the latest pay guide from the Fair Work Ombudsman for your specific classification.

faqs.q: Does the office administrator salary include superannuation?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of your salary. The super guarantee rate is 12% of ordinary earnings for 2026–27, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. For example, if your annual salary is $50,000, your employer must contribute an additional $6,000 into your super fund.

faqs.q: How is casual loading applied to an office administrator salary?
faqs.a: Casual employees are entitled to a 25% loading on top of the base hourly rate. For an office administrator earning $30 per hour, the casual rate would be $37.50 per hour. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave entitlements. When calculating annual salary for a casual, use the loaded rate in the formula: casual hourly rate × 38 × 52.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Office Administrator Salary Calculation

If you're an office administrator or considering a role, knowing how to convert your hourly rate into an annual salary is essential. The standard formula used across Australia is:

**Annual salary ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

This guide assumes a full-time working week of 38 ordinary hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman and the National Employment Standards. For part-time or casual work, adjust the weekly hours accordingly.

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is **$26.44 per hour**, or **$1,004.90 per week** for 38 hours, according to the Fair Work Commission. This is the minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. However, most office administrators are covered by an award—typically the **Clerks Award (MA000031)** or the **Professional Employees Award (MA000065)**. These awards set higher minimum rates depending on classification and experience.

For example, a Level 1 office administrator under the Clerks Award may earn a higher base rate than the national minimum. Always check the latest [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman for your specific role. The pay guides include all monetary allowances and the most frequently used penalty rates.

### From Hourly to Annual: The Formula

To estimate your annual office administrator salary, multiply your hourly rate by 38 (hours per week) and then by 52 (weeks per year).

**Example:**
- Hourly rate: $30.00
- Weekly: $30 × 38 = $1,140.00
- Annual: $1,140 × 52 = $59,280

This is your gross annual salary before tax and super. If you work fewer or more hours, adjust the weekly figure. For a fortnightly pay cycle, simply double the weekly amount: $1,140 × 2 = $2,280 per fortnight.

### Casual Loading and Its Effect

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of the base hourly rate. The Fair Work Ombudsman confirms this loading applies to award-free employees and most awards. For an office administrator earning $30 per hour base, the casual rate becomes $37.50 per hour. Use this loaded rate in the formula to estimate your annual salary.

**Important:** Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading into the calculator. Instead, enter the base hourly rate and check the casual loading box to have the 25% added automatically.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Your employer must pay superannuation guarantee contributions on top of your ordinary earnings. For 2026–27, the rate is **12%** of your gross salary, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830. This means if your annual office administrator salary is $60,000, your employer adds $7,200 to your super fund. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an additional cost to the employer.

### Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay depends on the 2026–27 resident tax rates and the Medicare levy. The tax-free threshold is $18,200. Above that, rates are:
- 15% from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% above $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. For a single person earning $59,280, tax would be approximately $8,442 plus Medicare $1,186, leaving a take-home of about $49,652 per year. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool for a detailed estimate.

### Comparing with Average Earnings

The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reported in May 2026 that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were **$2,083.70 per week**, or about $108,352 annually. All employees (including part-time) averaged $1,579.20 per week. An office administrator salary may be below this average, depending on experience and location. Check the [average pay](/topics/average-pay) page for more context.

### Award-Specific Considerations

Office administrators in the health or community sectors may fall under different awards. For example, the **Health Professionals and Support Services Award (MA000027)** or the **Social, Community, Home Care and Disability Services Industry Award (MA000100)** have their own classification structures and pay rates. The Fair Work Ombudsman has updated the SCHADS Award with increases from 1 December 2026. Always verify your award coverage using the [reference tables](/data) or the Pay and Conditions Tool.

### Using the Timesheet Calculator

Our [timesheet](/)（home page） allows you to enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. It then calculates your weekly, fortnightly, and annual gross pay, along with estimated tax and super. Remember that the results are estimates and do not include penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice arrangements.

### Key Points to Remember

- The formula assumes 38 hours per week, 52 weeks per year.
- Casual loading is 25% on top of the base rate.
- Super is 12% paid on top, not deducted from your salary.
- Tax is based on 2026–27 rates with the full tax-free threshold.
- Always check your award for minimum rates if you are covered by one.

For more details on the National Minimum Wage and award rates, visit the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page. If you need to convert a salary offer to an hourly rate, use the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool.
